name: Self-hosted who-dat instance (WHOIS/RDAP over HTTPS, setting whodat_url)
operator: The organisation running V3LUM: a who-dat instance it deploys itself (who-dat is MIT-licensed open-source software, github.com/Lissy93/who-dat)
tier_rationale: Instance operated by the organisation itself (P343 FC2 'a self-hosted who-dat instance (MIT) when the setting whodat_url is configured'); it relays the queried domain only to the registries' own RDAP/WHOIS servers, and internet registries are trusted (A8). Deliberately not 'internal': the value leaves the company towards the registries, so modules using it stay disclosure third_party and are never allowed at TLP:RED.

reliability.justification: Registry RDAP/WHOIS data normalised by who-dat (meta.source/meta.server name the registry server); the field mapping may lose detail, so registry values are never reinterpreted beyond the kept fields.

api.title: who-dat lookup GET <whodat_url>/<domain>: normalised registration data (registrar, dates, nameservers, status, DNSSEC, meta.source rdap|whois, meta.server)

terms.quote: Order: a self-hosted who-dat instance (MIT) when the setting whodat_url is configured, then direct port-43 WHOIS to the registry server taken from the IANA root-zone page (cached 7 days).

api.notes: Quote: binding council text (P343 FC2); research record C0785 'MIT (code); data from registries' RDAP/WHOIS'. Only https URLs count (hosts_from_settings); a configured host that another provider owns (e.g. the public who-dat.as93.net instance) is ignored, so the public instance can never be reached through this setting. Contact values are dropped at ingestion (P343 FC4); never CNPJ pivots (FC5).

notes: Owned by batch p2-G01-4 (P343 module whois_fallback). No key: an instance that answers 401 is reported 'could not verify' (V3LUM sends no credentials to it).
